data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from LSF)

# LSF requested:
#   -J all_to_all_32
#   -e all_to_all_32.%J.err
#   -o all_to_all_32.%J.out
#   -nnodes 32
#   -W 00:15

flux alloc \
  -N 32 \
  --time=15m \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate LSF %J with Flux job id.
exec >"all_to_all_32.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>"all_to_all_32.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

# NOTE: LSF job name (-J all_to_all_32) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

module load gcc
module load cuda/10.2.89
module load hwloc

cd /g/g14/bienz1/BenchPress/spectrum_build/examples

nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d

# NOTE: This workflow uses jsrun (IBM Spectrum LSF launcher). Flux does not provide a portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: if jsrun is not available/appropriate under Flux on your system, the job may fail to launch
# or may not use the allocated nodes/GPUs efficiently.
jsrun -a40 -c40 -g4 -r1 -n32 -M "-gpu" --latency_priority=gpu-cpu --launch_distribution=packed ./time_alltoall

echo quit | nvidia-cuda-mps-control
'
"
}
